### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.clue

### Question

I want to show keymaps for when I open `mini.pick` for example. So, I open a picker, then a `mini.clue` window with all the keymaps for `mini.pick` stays open until I pick something. Is there a way to achieve this?

Contributing guidelines

 I have read CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md

Module(s)
mini.clue
Question
I want to show keymaps for when I open mini.pick for example. So, I open a picker, then a mini.clue window with all the keymaps for mini.pick stays open until I pick something. Is there a way to achieve this?

comment_data.body:
I am afraid the answer is "No" to both larger and smaller questions.

The clue window is deliberately only shown [after pressing trigger key](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/5495dd5480843148b0e9ed57b42d32ea47ac2b52/doc/mini-clue.txt#L10). This is by design to limit the scope of the module and to have an explicit opt-in setup.

It is even more not capable of showing mappings in 'mini.pick' because it doesn't implement the regular Neovim/Vim mappings. It implements its own [mappings table](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/5495dd5480843148b0e9ed57b42d32ea47ac2b52/doc/mini-pick.txt#L467-L471) that defines which action to perform after pressing a single key. This behavior is due to how 'mini.pick' [implements its own key processing](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/5495dd5480843148b0e9ed57b42d32ea47ac2b52/doc/mini-pick.txt#L211-L214).

You can see all available mappings in a particular picker by pressing `<S-Tab>` (press `<S-Tab>` again to go back to main view; press `<C-f>` / `<C-b>` to scroll down/up).
